Executive Summary 
 
• Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%-
owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare 
earth carbonate (“MREC”). 
• Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 
Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 
ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026.  
• Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping 
Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, 
including: 
o  Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% 
o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% 
o  Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from 
commencement of operations 
o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion 
• Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting 
development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing 
operation.  
• Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with 
approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral 
Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant -
feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling.  
• The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral 
Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing 
substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine -life extension and/or 
expansion. 
• Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of-
mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of 
contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of 
approximately 58%. 
• Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, 
dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with 
yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. 
• Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate 
production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain 
subject to further evaluation. 
• Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 
100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding.
